headline: Economists and sociologists consulted by EL PAÍS say AI has not yet caused the mass job losses many people fear, though they warn about young graduates and inequality.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a thoughtful analysis with no new data, and its statistics are cited second-hand.
importance_line: A long analysis argues that mass AI job losses have not yet shown up in official figures, which matters to workers first, especially recent graduates, then governments weighing safety nets, but the figures are cited second-hand and the piece is analysis, not a new study.
summary: EL PAÍS English cites official US figures putting jobs created by AI in the past year at about one million and jobs lost at about 200,000, and a Stanford University study of job postings in 41 countries that found employment up 3.3% at the companies using AI most. The experts it quotes, including Nobel laureates Simon Johnson and Daron Acemoglu, say the nearer risks are fewer entry-level jobs for graduates and rising inequality, and agree that safety nets are needed.
notes: Full text read. Analysis feature; statistics not checked against their original sources.
